title: Revealing Pathway Interactions in Network Computations with Complete Path Contribution
abstract: arXiv:2611.26101v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Networks pass signals through many layers of interconnected units, so explaining what they compute means tracing how information travels from input to output and how pathways interact. Most existing approaches analyze only pairwise interactions between components such as units, layers or attention heads. Even when these measurements are combined post hoc into a circuit, they do not capture higher-order interactions along full causal chains (paths) from input to output, and so cannot address how exponentially many paths interact to construct network computation. This leaves a large set of mechanistic questions unanswerable, for example whether inhibitory pathways veto excitatory ones, and how the two combine to yield network decisions. translated_title: 利用完全路径贡献揭示网络计算中的通路相互作用
translated_abstract: 网络通过多层互联单元传递信号，因此解释网络计算意味着追踪信息如何从输入流向输出，以及各条通路之间如何相互作用。大多数现有方法仅分析单元、层或注意力头等组件之间的成对相互作用。即使将这些度量事后组合成电路，它们也无法捕捉从输入到输出的完整因果链（路径）上的高阶相互作用，因此无法解答指数级数量的路径如何相互作用以构建网络计算。这使得大量机制性问题无法回答，例如抑制性通路是否会否决兴奋性通路，以及两者如何结合以产生网络决策。为了填补这一空白，我们提出了完全路径贡献，这是一种将网络输出分解为各条路径的数学上完整的贡献的方法，从而可以直接研究路径层面的相互作用。
tldr: 该论文提出“完全路径贡献”方法，将网络输出分解为每条路径在数学上完整的贡献，从而能够直接分析从输入到输出的完整因果路径之间的高阶相互作用。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes Complete Path Contribution, a method that decomposes network output into mathematically complete contributions of individual paths, enabling direct analysis of higher-order interactions along full causal pathways in network computations.
